title: 2606.09842v1
universal_lens: Human pose estimation via vision unifies model-based kinematics with deep learning architectures, bridging explicit body models and end-to-end feature extraction through probabilistic inference. MediaPipe-based pose estimation enables low-latency, cross-platform edge deployment for real-time exercise repetition counting via keypoint tracking and kinematic state transitions.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian hierarchical models to integrate pose estimates with athletic performance metrics, enabling conformal uncertainty quantification across motion capture data streams. Bayesian inference framework maps pose landmarks to probabilistic exercise states using conformal prediction for reliable repetition counts under uncertainty.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes temporal state transitions to model athlete behavior dynamics, mapping pose sequences into actionable feedback loops that adapt to real-time biomechanical constraints. Situationally-aware state-transition engine models exercise kinematics through temporal keypoint sequences, enabling dynamic feedback and adaptive coaching protocols.

reasoning_traces.think:
The derivation within this chapter window establishes the rigorous bridge between raw computer vision outputs and actionable biomechanical intelligence. Starting from the fundamental Joint Angle Calculation (Primitive 1), we define the state space \mathcal{S} as a manifold of joint configurations A, B, C \in \mathbb{R}^2. However, raw pixel coordinates are inherently noisy. Therefore, the Frame-to-Frame Jitter Metric (Primitive 3) acts as a necessary regularization term, employing a rolling standard deviation \sigma_{jitter} to filter high-frequency stochastic noise introduced by the MediaPipe inference pass. This ensures that the underlying kinematic signal remains smooth, a prerequisite for accurate derivative-based analysis.

Simultaneously, the Temporal Segmentation Kernel (Primitive 4) operates on these smoothed angular trajectories \theta(t). By identifying zero-crossings or velocity peaks exceeding \lambda_{thresh}, the system discretizes continuous time into meaningful exercise repetitions N_{reps}. This discretization is not merely counting; it defines the boundaries for localized Bayesian inference within GSI, allowing the model to isolate specific movement flaws without contamination from adjacent cycles.

Crucially, all these mathematical operations are bounded by the Latency Budget Constraint (Primitive 2). The requirement that P(L_{e2e} \leq 45ms) \geq 0.95 imposes a strict computational topology. It forces the choice of lightweight operators and limits the window size W in the jitter calculation. If the inference pipeline violates this constraint, the feedback loop desynchronizes from the athlete's physical reality, rendering the generated language model insights obsolete. Thus, the mathematical formulation is not just descriptive but prescriptive, dictating the architectural limits of the Galaxy Sports Engine to ensure real-time viability under varied lighting and occlusion conditions.
reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive lineage traces back to early biomechanical optoelectronics (e.g., Vicon systems) which relied on physical markers and offline processing. The shift to marker-less, real-time estimation via MediaPipe democratizes access but introduces new stochastic errors. Our primitives mathematically reconcile the historical demand for millimeter-level precision with the probabilistic nature of modern deep learning inference, evolving from deterministic rigid-body dynamics to probabilistic state estimation under strict latency constraints.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the athlete (the opposing agent), the system must anticipate their intent to maximize performance while minimizing cognitive load. The athlete does not perceive MPJPE or latency percentiles; they perceive 'smoothness' and 'immediate relevance'. The GSE models this by translating low-level jitter metrics into high-level confidence scores. If the system detects high uncertainty (e.g., occluded fingers), it suppresses granular feedback to avoid confusing the user, instead focusing on gross motor patterns. This mirrors a coach's intuition: knowing when to intervene and when to let the flow continue.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent catastrophic failure, we implement strict anti-collinearity vetoes. If the joint coordinates A, B, C become collinear (full extension), the angle calculation yields a singularity. Furthermore, if the latency L_{e2e} breaches the 45ms threshold, a hard veto triggers, bypassing the complex language model and defaulting to a simple visual blink to indicate system overload. This prevents the generation of hallucinated feedback based on stale or geometrically invalid data, ensuring the integrity of the sovereign primitive stack.
